findings.title: Credential key saved as safeParse result wrapper
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturn object `{success, data}`, not the parsed data. Before this change the code stored the output of `googleCredentialSchema.parse`. Now the whole wrapper is written to credential.key, so the stored credential becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}`. The next googleCredentialSchema.parse of that key fails and Google Calendar breaks after the first token refresh.

findings.title: Sync endpoint fetch Response has no .data
findings.body: When syncing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads `res?.data` (the gaxios shape). `token` is undefined, so `token.access_token` throws. Hubspot, zoho-bigin and zohocrm have the same problem: they read `.data` or token fields directly from the return value instead of calling `.json()`.

findings.title: prisma used without import
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but this file never imports prisma. The call throws a ReferenceError at runtime, which breaks every Salesforce client creation.

findings.title: Token refreshed on every client construction; new token unused
findings.body: getClient refreshes the token unconditionally on every instantiation. It also bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so sync mode is ignored here. It then builds the connection with the old `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the freshly fetched one.

findings.title: Bogus zod schema keys
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse to that same string, so the schema actually requires a property named "[object Object]". The intent was to accept any numeric expiry field, but in sync mode valid responses fail validation.

findings.title: Overwrites missing refresh_token with literal placeholder
findings.body: When the response has no refresh_token, it is set to the string "refresh_token". That placeholder gets persisted to the DB as the credential's refresh token, so later refreshes against the real provider fail. Separately, office365 previously tolerated parse failures, but the function now throws on them.

findings.title: credentialId passed as userId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, but this call passes credentialId. The sync endpoint is therefore asked for tokens belonging to whatever user happens to have that id, which can fetch the wrong user's credentials.

findings.title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
findings.body: The app slug is "zoom" (the credential is created with appId "zoom"), but the sync request sends "zoomvideo". The self-hoster's endpoint won't recognize this slug.

findings.title: Non-constant-time secret compare; parse errors return 500
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret. Separately, zod `parse` and `JSON.parse` of the decrypted keys throw on bad input, so malformed requests return 500 instead of 400.

findings.title: Sync endpoint call unauthenticated, unchecked
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no secret header, so the self-hoster's endpoint cannot verify the caller and anyone can request user tokens from it. The response status is also never checked, so error responses are treated as token payloads.
